title: The Educated Barbarian: Book of Five Rings analysis (part. 6)
summary: Sixth installment of his reading of Musashi's Book of Five Rings, applied to lifting and life. He argues that body and mind must be trained together, that freedom from 'self' (living for one's image) underpins unbreakable discipline, and draws lessons on crossing at a ford, rhythm, influence ('infecting' others with spirit) and keeping balance against danger, hardship and surprise.

claims.claim: The mental capacities built through lifting carry over to the rest of life; training daily built his discipline and made him a better person outside the gym.
People who skip lifting to focus on intellectual development are misguided: a strong body helps build a strong spirit and vice versa, and neither can be trained alone very far.
Training 10 hours a day without ever reading or thinking is also imbalance and won't even produce proper gains; you need the alliance of body and spirit.
Theory-only fitness bores him: studies, writing and theories are worthless if never applied with your own body; you should both think about strategy and apply it.
The 'self' is the image you present to others; it becomes a problem when it replaces your soul and you start living for others' approval instead of pursuing your path.
If you live for the approval of a crowd, you become like that crowd, including its malice; integrity means staying true to yourself whoever surrounds you.
Don't train for others; once you find your calling, others' opinions stop affecting you and insecurity disappears.
Musashi's 'miraculous power' is, for him, an unbreakable discipline and control of the mind, which anyone can develop simply by training.

In high school he trained every day, leaving friends to go home and train; they couldn't understand doing something painful with no reward, especially since he was skinny and weak and progressed slower than most.
The strength of mind he built as a slow-progressing skinny teen made up for his slow physical progress.

If you have a real goal you will be surrounded by people who don't share it, don't understand it, or don't want you to succeed ('crabs in a bucket'), because your success removes their excuses for mediocrity; set sail anyway.
You need to know the destination even if you don't know the exact route; the path is discovered along the way, but without a clear goal you can't stay on it.
Knowing 'the soundness of your ship' means knowing how your body responds to training, technique and form, which prevents injury and keeps you lifting long-term.
Day-to-day readiness varies; be adaptable within your program to do the maximum you can each day without overreaching.

Life's hardships are rivers to cross; charging straight across without thinking brings defeats that can stop you forever, while seeking the ford (the weak point where your strength suffices) lets you keep crossing for life.
When conditions are against you, turn back or wait rather than fight the wind; but when the goal is within reach and only effort separates defeat from victory, row.

Rhythm is distinct from speed and strength; a football receiver who isn't fastest or strongest but runs routes with good rhythm is favored by the quarterback, and the best defender is the one who matches that rhythm.

In bodybuilding, rhythm means staying disciplined and having a program rhythm that carries your progress; injuries like a hurt tendon or life events break it and you collapse, so avoid them where possible.
Never assume others have mastered something beyond your reach; learn from them and tell yourself that if they got there, you can too.
When confronted by people trying to rob him, treating them as friends defused the situation every time; he once got would-be phone thieves to guide him through their neighborhood.
In a potential mugging, showing fear or pretending nothing is happening hands them the upper hand; inject a friendly spirit rather than aggression, since the other person might be unhinged.

Danger, hardship and surprise break your balance; mentally rehearsing a scenario once (e.g. a loved one attacked) prepares you without needing to dwell on it, avoiding anxiety while keeping balance and rhythm.

Many people are unhappy without knowing why because their spirit has been replaced by others' influence; those who influence you mostly don't have your interests at heart, and the media is the biggest culprit.
Even if you're not manipulative, study how influence works so you can protect your own integrity and help others regain theirs.
